name: EgoHumans
description: We present EgoHumans, a new multi-view multi-human video benchmark to advance the state-of-the-art of egocentric human 3D pose estimation and tracking. Existing egocentric benchmarks either capture single subject or indoor-only scenarios, which limit the generalization of computer vision algorithms for real-world applications. We propose a novel 3D capture setup to construct a comprehensive egocentric multi-human benchmark in the wild with annotations to support diverse tasks such as human detection, tracking, 2D/3D pose estimation, and mesh recovery. We leverage consumer-grade wearable camera-equipped glasses for the egocentric view, which enables us to capture dynamic activities like playing tennis, fencing, volleyball, etc. Furthermore, our multi-view setup generates accurate 3D ground truth even under severe or complete occlusion. The dataset consists of more than 125k egocentric images, spanning diverse scenes with a particular focus on challenging and unchoreographed multi-human activities and fast-moving egocentric views. We rigorously evaluate existing state-of-the-art methods and highlight their limitations in the egocentric scenario, specifically on multi-human tracking.  To address such limitations, we propose EgoFormer, a novel approach with a multi-stream transformer architecture and explicit 3D spatial reasoning to estimate and track the human pose. EgoFormer significantly outperforms prior art by 13.6% IDF1 on the EgoHumans dataset.
evaluation_method: task-specific metrics (e.g., mAP for detection, IDF1 for tracking, MPJPE / PCK for 3D/2D pose)
general_score_metric: IDF1 (for tracking); MPJPE / PCK (for pose estimation)
reputation: A recent, high-quality egocentric multi-human benchmark that has attracted attention in the egocentric pose and tracking research community but is not yet a widespread standard.
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark with ~125k egocentric images; focuses on challenging in-the-wild multi-human and fast-motion scenarios, potential privacy concerns from wearable cameras, and significant occlusion making tasks difficult.
